## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the security change holds in the tested scope. No string accepted by `launch_command_is_safe` made `eval "set -- ..."` run anything other than `set`. Every in-repo caller format produces the same argv as before, and the new test passes on this head and fails against the previous script. Three smaller points follow: an unreachable duplicate `case` arm, a compatibility claim in the description that is broader than the code, and a behavior change for focused webapp URLs.

**Verified** base versus head, with `hyprctl` and `setsid` mocked:

```text
launch string                                   base (eval exec setsid)        head
uwsm-app -- foot                                [uwsm-app] [--] [foot]         same
omarchy-launch-tui zsh -c 'fastfetch; read -k 1'  4 args, quoted ; kept          same
nautilus "$HOME/Documents"                      $HOME expanded                 same
foot $(touch MARKER)                            MARKER created                 refused, nothing runs
foot `touch MARKER`                             MARKER created                 refused, nothing runs
foo z*.txt  (file named "z|touch MARKER|.txt")  glob result re-parsed, MARKER  one literal argument
```

The validator's rules match the Bash 5.3 lexer (metacharacters, blanks, word-start `#` comments, backslash-newline removal, `$(`, `${`, `$[`, `$'`, `$"`). A fuzz of 406,200 generated strings (32,309 accepted) found no accepted string that executed a command, with positive and negative detector controls behaving as expected.

### Duplicate `"\\")` case arm is unreachable

`bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus` has two consecutive `"\\")` arms. Bash runs the first matching arm, so the second (lines 39-48) never executes. It came from commit `42ec8081` and still sets `word_start=1` on backslash-newline, the behavior that the final commit removed from the live arm.

**Impact:** no runtime effect today. A later edit could land in the dead arm and appear to change behavior without doing so.

**Suggested change:** delete the second `"\\")` arm.

### Some non-executing forms that used to launch are now refused

The description says quoting and `$HOME`/`~` semantics "match the previous eval exactly; only strings that could run a second command are now refused". Plain `$HOME` and `~` do behave as before. These forms, which cannot start a second command, are now refused:

```text
${HOME}/Downloads          brace-form expansion (plain $HOME still works)
$'a\tb'  $"text"           ANSI-C and locale quoting
$?  $#  $@                 special parameters
foo$   "bar$"              a $ at the end or before a quote or space
foo >/dev/null   foo &     single-command redirection, trailing &
foo<newline>               unquoted newline (previously treated as a space)
```

Whitespace inside quotes is now also kept exactly as written, where the old code collapsed it (for example `zsh -c 'echo  two   spaces'`). That is an improvement, but it is also a difference from the old behavior.

**Impact:** no in-repo caller uses these forms. A user binding that does, for example `${HOME}` in a launch command, or a single-argument call such as `omarchy-launch-or-focus '^signal$'` whose default launch command becomes `uwsm-app -- ^signal$`, now does not launch. The refusal is written only to stderr, and the Lua binding helper shows no notification, so from a keybinding the failure is likely silent (not observed in a live session).

**Suggested change:** describe the refused forms in the PR description. Optional approaches: accept the strict `${NAME}` form, which is as safe as `$NAME`, and surface the refusal with a notification as well as stderr.

### Focused webapp URLs containing `&` or `;` now launch nothing

`bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus-webapp` (unchanged by this PR) still builds `LAUNCH_COMMAND="omarchy-launch-webapp $@"` without re-quoting. The Lua helper quotes the URL for the outer call only, so shell syntax in the URL reaches the inner parse:

```text
URL in a focus=true webapp binding   base                               head
https://e.test/?a=1&b=2              launches truncated ...?a=1          refused, nothing launches
https://e.test/a;b                   launches truncated .../a            refused, nothing launches
https://e.test/a(b)                  eval syntax error, no launch        refused, nothing launches
```

**Impact:** the shipped `focus = true` webapp bindings contain none of these characters, and the shipped URL with `&` does not go through this wrapper. Custom focused webapp URLs with query strings change from a truncated launch to no launch. Neither version preserves such URLs; the limitation predates this PR.

**Suggested change:** quote each forwarded argument for the inner launch string, for example `printf -v LAUNCH_COMMAND '%q ' omarchy-launch-webapp "$@"`. In an isolated diagnostic copy of the wrapper, this passed URLs containing `&`, `;`, `(`, `'`, `$` and spaces through unchanged; only an embedded newline was still refused. The TUI wrapper can keep its plain join, since its argument is meant to be a command line.

**Optional test improvement:** `grep -E '^eval[[:space:]]' ... && fail` also passes on the previous script, because its `eval` line was indented, so only the first grep distinguishes old from new code. The final "execute nothing" check only looks at `$sandbox_dir/pwned`, which only the `;` and `&&` payloads target, and those did not run under the old code either (`exec` replaced the shell first). The payloads that did run under the old code (`$(...)`, backticks, `|`) write to a literal `/tmp/pwned` that is never checked. Pointing every payload at `$sandbox_dir/pwned` makes that check meaningful and keeps a regression from writing outside the sandbox.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the changed files, all in-repo callers and the GNU Bash 5.3 parser source. Isolated command-only runs on Bash 5.3.15 with mocked `hyprctl` and `setsid`: the PR test on head and against the previous script, a 67-case base/head differential, a generated-string fuzz with controls, and a diagnostic copy of the webapp wrapper. Not tested: a live Hyprland session (including where a refusal's stderr appears), non-UTF-8 multibyte locales, and Bash patch-level differences in the lexer beyond 5.3 patchlevel 0 source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check. The duplicate arm, the refused forms and the webapp behavior were identified independently by one assessment and confirmed from source by the other.
